Ford Had Another Name for the Mustang Dark Horse SC, Changed It Because It Was Weird
17 photos
Photo: Ford
Ford had a different name chosen for what we know today as the Mustang Dark Horse SC. The automaker had already filed trademarks for the designation in Europe and the United States. However, a last-minute decision sent the muscle car to the market with a different name than originally planned.
The original name choice for what we know as the Ford Mustang Dark Horse SC was Dark Horse Boss. Ford was ready to use it after filing trademarks for it long before the model went into production at the Flat Rock Assembly Plant in Flat Rock, Michigan, along with its Mustang siblings.
Instead, Ford moved forward into its new modern performance branding and chose the Mustang Dark Horse SC name, where the "SC" serves as a nod to the supercharged Predator V8 engine, roaring from under the hood. The choice aligns with Ford CEO Jim Farley’s naming strategy to avoid over-relying on nostalgic nameplates like the "Boss" or "Cobra," going instead in a forward-looking direction with the Mustang.
Ford also deliberately chose to drop the legendary Shelby nameplate for this GT500-level successor. Back in January, at the Detroit Motor Show, Jim Farley clarified that the car is built by the automaker’s own racing division.
Photo: Ford " This is a Ford Racing car, and the reality is that Shelby doesn't race. Our idea is for Ford Racing to actually develop road vehicles. They will develop our next-generation supercars, " he explained at the time. Furthermore, the Shelby brand no longer aligns with the customer demographic that Ford is after with muscle cars such as the Mustang Dark Horse SC.
Sources confirmed to Ford Authority that Ford's executives ultimately dropped the idea because combining the words created the phrase "Horse Boss." The team decided the combination sounded far too awkward for a performance vehicle and scrapped it.
The Dark Horse SC is the second-most powerful production Mustang ever built and the only one that is not light-years behind the almighty Mustang GTD and far above the non-SC Dark Horse. It comes with the 5.2-liter cross-plane crank Predator V8 with supercharged firepower.
While the non-SC version has to resort to 500 horsepower (507 metric horsepower) and 418 pound-feet (567 Newton meters) of torque, coming out of its Coyote 5.0-liter naturally aspirated V8, the Dark Horse SC boasts 795 horsepower (806 metric horsepower) and 660 pound-feet (895 Newton meters).
Photo: Ford Those are enough to make the Mustang Dark Horse SC rocket from zero to hero (0 to 60 mph or 0 to 97 kph) in just 2.9 seconds, run the quarter mile in 10.8 seconds with a trap speed of 131.8 mph, and max out at 180 mph (289 kph). For all these, customers pay a starting price of $106,585.
